mismatch.message: C begins the Excalibur blessing message; JS exits through UnsupportedFountainError

summary: The admitted lawful Knight level-7 session dips a single rusty nonartifact long sword into a fountain. At step 121 C succeeds in dipfountain's Excalibur branch after rn2(6)=0 and displays the Lady of the Lake message; JS consumes the same draw but throws UnsupportedFountainError before any branch effect. Implement the complete fountain.c:dipfountain function and keep its existing potion.c:dodip production call aligned; do not claim the entire fountain.c file.

source.branch: fountain.c:dipfountain 404-447: LONG_SWORD, u.ulevel >= 5, successful role-dependent rn2, quan==1, nonartifact and no existing Excalibur. A lawful hero receives the artifact; a nonlawful hero is denied and cursed. Both outcomes update inventory, remove the fountain, redraw it, optionally anger town guards, and return. The selected case reaches the lawful Knight success branch.

evidence: The admitted v53 manifest identifies the route as fountain.c:dipfountain through potion.c:dodip:404-447, with a lawful Knight at level 7 dipping a single nonartifact long sword.

The saved accepted baseline hosted-38314809018-1-v53.json records 121/300 screens, 3112/3259 RNG values and 121/300 cursors matched. The immutable recording's step 121 is the first unmatched screen and includes rn2(6)=0 @ dipfountain(fountain.c:405); its C output begins 'From the murky depths, a hand reaches up to bless the sword.' The next C step begins 'As the hand retreats, the fountain disappears!'.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/potion.c:dodip calls dipfountain(obj) after confirming the player accepted dipping into a fountain. The existing JS potion.js:dodip already calls dipfountain(obj,state,env).

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/fountain.c:404-447 contains both lawful-success and nonlawful-denial outcomes and the shared fountain-removal/update path. JS js/fountain.js:927-940 consumes the matching rn2 draw and then throws UnsupportedFountainError instead of executing those C outcomes.

The implementation task is a whole dipfountain function port because this is missing source behavior, not a defect in an otherwise implemented branch. Existing caller wiring is to be retained and verified; no whole-file fountain.c completion is claimed.
